q: There are at least ____ different organic compounds currently on the planet and every one of them is unique in its chemical structure and specific properties.
e: There are at least ten million different organic compounds currently on the planet and every one of them is unique in its chemical structure and specific properties. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond.

q: The ____ atom is central to all organic compounds.
e: The carbon atom is central to all organic compounds. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond.

q: Organic compounds contain carbon and hydrogen in which there is at least one ____ or C-H bond and sometimes a few other elements such as oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, phosphorus and the halogens.
e: Organic compounds contain carbon and hydrogen in which there is at least one C-C or C-H bond and sometimes a few other elements such as oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, phosphorus and the halogens. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. Organic chemistry is built on carbon-hydrogen frameworks with covalent bonds. The organic definition used here needs at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond.

q: The bonding patterns of carbon with its valence of ____ form single, double and triple bonds.
e: The bonding patterns of carbon with its valence of four form single, double and triple bonds. Listen for four in that sentence.

q: Carbon forms a large number of compounds with hydrogen which are collectively called ____.
e: Carbon forms a large number of compounds with hydrogen which are collectively called hydrocarbons. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds.

q: Hydrocarbons are compounds in which carbon and hydrogen atoms bonded to each other by ____ bonds.
e: Hydrocarbons are compounds in which carbon and hydrogen atoms bonded to each other by covalent bonds. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms. Organic chemistry is built on carbon-hydrogen frameworks with covalent bonds.

q: The hydrocarbon compounds that contain only single bonds are called saturated hydrocarbons, and are classified as ____.
e: The hydrocarbon compounds that contain only single bonds are called saturated hydrocarbons, and are classified as alkanes. Hydrocarbons with only carbon-carbon single bonds are saturated. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds.

q: Those that contain double or triple bonds are called ____ hydrocarbons which include alkenes, alkynes and aromatic compounds.
e: Those that contain double or triple bonds are called unsaturated hydrocarbons which include alkenes, alkynes and aromatic compounds. Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, so alkenes, alkynes and aromatics sit in that group. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.

q: The ____ formula is used to represent the families of organic compounds.
e: The general formula is used to represent the families of organic compounds. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once.

q: The ____ formula of an organic compound is the actual number of atoms of each element present in a molecule.
e: The molecular formula of an organic compound is the actual number of atoms of each element present in a molecule. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. The molecular formula gives the actual number of each kind of atom in one molecule.

q: A ____ structural formula (graphic formula or displayed formula) shows every bond and atom in what order atoms are attached, but does not portray accurately the three-dimensional geometry of the molecule.
e: A full structural formula (graphic formula or displayed formula) shows every bond and atom in what order atoms are attached, but does not portray accurately the three-dimensional geometry of the molecule. A structural formula shows which atoms are attached to which, not just the count of each element. A full structural formula draws every bond and atom so you can see the arrangement.

q: A ____ structural formula is a more compact way of drawing the structural formula of a molecule.
e: A condensed structural formula is a more compact way of drawing the structural formula of a molecule. A structural formula shows which atoms are attached to which, not just the count of each element. A condensed structural formula still shows the order of groups but hides many of the individual bonds.

q: Organic compounds are classified according to the different types of ____ groups.
e: Organic compounds are classified according to the different types of functional groups. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: An alkane is a compound that lacks ____ groups.
e: An alkane is a compound that lacks functional groups. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: The functional group in an alkene is a carbon-carbon ____ bond.
e: The functional group in an alkene is a carbon-carbon double bond. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: The functional group in an alkyne is a carbon-carbon ____ bond.
e: The functional group in an alkyne is a carbon-carbon triple bond. Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon triple bond and the general formula CnH2n-2. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: A functional group is an atom or a group or atoms that determine the ____ properties of a compound.
e: A functional group is an atom or a group or atoms that determine the chemical properties of a compound. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: An alcohol is an organic compound with a ____ (-OH) functional group attached to a carbon atom.
e: An alcohol is an organic compound with a hydroxyl (-OH) functional group attached to a carbon atom. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: Alcohols can often be represented by the general formula ROH, where R is an ____ group.
e: Alcohols can often be represented by the general formula ROH, where R is an alkyl group. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once.

q: A ____ series is a group of organic compounds, usually listed in order of increasing size, that have the same functional group and similar structure.
e: A homologous series is a group of organic compounds, usually listed in order of increasing size, that have the same functional group and similar structure. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: In a homologous series, all the compounds differ only by the number of ____ units in the main carbon chain.
e: In a homologous series, all the compounds differ only by the number of CH_2 units in the main carbon chain. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2.

q: In a homologous series, all the compounds fit the same ____ formula.
e: In a homologous series, all the compounds fit the same general formula. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once.

q: As the chain gets longer, the compounds show a ____ change in properties.
e: As the chain gets longer, the compounds show a gradual change in properties. Listen for gradual in that sentence.
